channel.title: SolidCraft CAD – CAD models
channel.description: Recent content in CAD models on SolidCraft CAD

item.title: MFT Rail Corner Assembly
item.description: Standalone qualification assembly for issue #62. Two 150 mm MountingRailM8 pieces meet at 90 degrees with their C-openings facing outward. The dark printable bracket sits in the inside corner and continues underneath both rail ends as a 6 mm load-bearing foot. A low rounded plastic nose protects the exposed outside corner below the channels. Its four Ø8.5 rail holes align with the first and second round perforations on the two galvanized profiles, while the top gusset exposes one provisional screw seat toward the future MFT underside.

item.title: MFT Rail Corner Bracket
item.description: Prototype monolithic corner bracket for the Simple MFT support frame. Two perpendicular 75 mm arms bolt through the existing round rail perforations at 12.5 mm and 62.5 mm from each rail end. Two 6 mm-thick plastic shoes continue underneath the rail profiles so the rails actually rest on the bracket. Those shoes merge into a low 22 mm-radius rounded outside-corner bumper that projects beyond the sharp metal corner without blocking the C-openings. Upper and lower triangular gussets stiffen the corner. The upper gusset includes one provisional countersunk fixing hole into the underside of the MFT worktop.

item.title: BasicHub75Screen
item.description: Five panels on the source project’s 800 × 320 mm nominal grid. One reusable detailed panel component is reused at X=-320, -160, 0, 160 and 320 mm. Columns 2 and 4 reverse direction for the rear data chain, and all occurrences stand upright in XZ.

item.title: Hub75DisplayCase
item.description: One clearly parametrized assembly: five lightweight HUB75 modules, 12 mm sidewalls/bottom/roof, 9 mm attached rear, 4 mm glass and four straight-mitred wooden retainers from one GlassStrip class. The roof extends 10 mm in front and 1 mm beyond the attached rear sheet. Eight printed corner brackets share the CornerBracket definition.

item.title: Hub75DisplayCase v2
item.description: Second-generation wooden HUB75 enclosure. It keeps the 844 × 362 mm display opening and five-panel layout while adding a 70 mm clear lower compartment, a 12 mm intermediate shelf, two 12 mm dividers, full-depth side walls with hand slots, and an inset display-only rear board.

item.title: Simple MFT assembly
item.description: The 805 mm Simple MFT worktop is extended on the right by a plain 195 × 555 × 18 mm plank, creating a 1000 mm-wide work surface. Two long M8 mounting rails run underneath and are shifted 18 mm right to meet a third 519 mm cross rail on the left short side without blocking the channel ends. All C-openings face outward. The 800 mm Festool-profile GuideRail is shifted 414 mm toward +X. A reusable FlexBenchDog is inserted in the bottom hole of the rightmost MFT column at X=+304 mm, Y=-228 mm. MDF, galvanized-steel and aluminium materials distinguish the assembly visually.

item.title: FlexBenchDog
item.description: A printable bench dog inferred from the Mini-MFT reference image: 20 mm above and 20 mm below the worktop, with one full-length tapered insert from Ø20.0 at the worktop to Ø20.2 at the free end. A compact Ø22 stop collar seats on the 45° chamfer of a nominal Ø20 MFT hole. Two perpendicular slots create four flexible legs, with R0.5 mm relief around the central cross. The top face carries a recessed BrainBox cube/box wireframe.

item.title: GuideRail — Festool profile
item.description: The generic GuideRail component with its default Festool profile. The aluminium cross-section comes from the FS 1400/2 STEP reference and is calibrated to the TSO measured 184.20 × 10.50 mm envelope. Only rail length is a native CAD parameter.

item.title: GuideRail — Makita profile
item.description: A second fixed cross-section of the generic GuideRail component. The aluminium shape comes from the Makita 199141-8 STEP reference and is calibrated to the TSO measured 182.50 × 10.28 mm envelope. The standalone CAD example uses 600 mm for compact visual inspection.

item.title: Mounting Rail M8
item.description: A reusable light mounting-rail component authored in fabrication order as native sheet metal: developed flat blank, four source perforations, one repeated native feature pattern and four 90-degree folds. The supplied DRESSELHAUS/HORNBACH product establishes 1000 mm length, galvanized steel, M8 use and 1.25 mm thickness. The 27 × 18 mm section and perforation dimensions use a generic published 27/18 rail reference and are not claimed as DRESSELHAUS manufacturing dimensions.

item.title: Simple MFT
item.description: A reusable CRAFTMAKER-inspired worktop component: one 18 mm native Box, four straight 20 mm corner chamfers, 59 Ø20 dog holes on the nominal 9 × 7 / 76 mm grid with the four diagonal ring-2 positions omitted, and eight photo-measured native diagonal Slots.

item.title: CornerBracket
item.description: One shared CornerBracket is reused by the standalone model and wooden HUB75 assemblies. Its native outline includes the 0.6 mm arm-tip relief, with inner R4 fillet, broad-face chamfers and four local triangular arm-tip wedge cuts kept editable. Four fixing seats use separate flat head recess, 90° transition, through-bore and 0.2 mm edge-relief features instead of one oversized countersink.

item.title: Hub75Panel
item.description: Shared panel component from the existing OpenSCAD reference: a 159.70 × 319.71 × 14.50 mm envelope with four rear pockets, six rear-side Ø3 bores in Ø8.5 mounting tubes, separate rear reinforcement features, two locator pins and a grey housing material. Standalone uses the component’s own local XY/Z axes; screen assemblies rotate the exact same class into world XZ.

item.title: Bolted Flange
item.description: A compact primitive model: Ø100 × 10 flange, Ø44 × 16 hub, Ø24 bore and six Ø9 bolt holes on a 70 mm PCD.

item.title: Plastic Enclosure
item.description: Rebuilds the supplied enclosure with the normal SCPF Box sketch/extrusion, followed by native Shell, Lip, Snap Fit, Boss and Rest features.

item.title: Plastic Enclosure Pi
item.description: Reconstructs the Raspberry Pi 4 video using a rounded open-top shell, mounting bosses, connector cuts, floor vents, Pi 4 lettering and PETG material.

item.title: Simple Box
item.description: Minimal model proving that one independent model root can be authored with Forge and built without repository-specific Python orchestration.

item.title: Bracket
item.description: An XZ polygon extruded along Y with an edge fillet and two native SolidCraft Hole features.

item.title: CsgCube
item.description: A constructive solid geometry demonstration: intersect a cube with a sphere, then subtract cylinders along three axes.

item.title: SamplePlate
item.description: Builds a centered plate with native Base, Holes and Bore sketches. One parameter-driven Ø8 hole cut is repeated by a native rectangular pattern, while a Ø24 boss is joined between the two cuts.

item.title: Vent Plate
item.description: Recreates the SolidCraft Vent Plate example with a rounded 120 × 80 × 4 mm plate, one rectangular source cut and one native two-direction rectangular pattern.

item.title: Plate
item.description: A feature-based plate: box, four vertical fillets and four through holes.
